title: Senior asks: reserveFreeName() uses fopen($path, 'x'). The file already exists. What does fopen return?
options: false, and a warning (the @ hides it)
A handle that overwrites the file
A handle to the end of the file
explain: Mode 'x' creates the file only if it does not exist, in one atomic step. If it exists, fopen returns false and gives a warning. So two uploads at the same time cannot get the same name. file_exists() then fopen() would have a race between the two calls.

title: Senior asks: a user writes the row ['a,b', 'say "hi"'] to a CSV file. What does fputcsv() write?
explain: fputcsv() wraps a field in quotes when it has a comma, a quote or a line break. A quote inside is doubled. This is the CSV standard, and read() with SplFileObject understands it back. Never build CSV lines with implode(',').

title: Senior asks: CsvFileActions reads with SplFileObject and READ_CSV. The file is "id,fruit\n1,apple\n". How many fields does each row have?
code:
<?php
$p = tempnam(sys_get_temp_dir(), 'c');
file_put_contents($p, "id,fruit\n1,apple\n");
$f = new SplFileObject($p);
$f->setFlags(SplFileObject::READ_CSV);
foreach ($f as $row) echo count($row), ' ';
unlink($p);
explain: The text ends with a newline, so SplFileObject gives one more row after the last line. It is [null], one field. Without the flags SKIP_EMPTY, READ_AHEAD and DROP_NEW_LINE you must skip this row yourself, or you get a wrong 'column count' error.

title: Senior asks: your tests write to sys_get_temp_dir() with fixed names and call unlink() at the end of the test. One assert fails in the middle. What is the problem?
options: unlink() never runs, so the file stays and the next run can fail or pass by mistake
Nothing: PHPUnit deletes the files itself
The test cannot fail, because the name is fixed
explain: A failed assert stops the test, so cleanup code after it is skipped. Use setUp() and tearDown() for files, and make the name unique (tempnam() or a random suffix). Then every run starts clean, also when tests run in parallel.

title: What does Node print?
explain: sort() without a function compares the items as strings: '1' < '10' < '9'. For numbers always pass a compare function: sort((a, b) => a - b). Also, sort() changes the array in place.

title: PHP 8. B extends A and does not declare its own $n. What does this print?
code:
<?php
class A { public static int $n = 0; }
class B extends A {}
B::$n++;
echo A::$n;
explain: A static property is shared with child classes unless the child declares it again. B::$n and A::$n are the same variable. If each class needs its own counter, redeclare it in the child.

title: You ran git add a.php. Then you edited a.php again. What does plain `git diff` show?
options: Only the second edit (not yet staged)
explain: git diff compares the working tree with the index (staged). So it shows only changes you have not staged. Use git diff --staged to see what the next commit will contain. Check both before you commit.

title: PHP 8. A search box sends an empty string. What does this print?
explain: Since PHP 8 an empty needle is always found: str_contains() returns true. So a filter like `if (str_contains($name, $q))` shows every item when $q is empty. Check for an empty $q first if you do not want that.
